newsitem.title: INDIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - April 4.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - April 4.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Indian business and political stories in leading newspapers prepared for REUTERS by Business News and Information Services Pvt Ltd, New Delhi Tel:3324842, 3351006, 3761233 Fax:+91-11-3351006 Internet: biznis@giasbm01.vsnl.net.in
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
TOP STORIES
The Times Of India
UNITED FRONT NOT READY FOR GOVERNMENT WITHOUT GOWDA

The ruling United Front (UF) said it was prepared to discuss a structured coordination on policy issues, an understanding on specific programmes and perhaps electoral adjustments in the future with the Congress. However, there was no question of either changing their leader, Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda, or sharing power with the Congress. The Congress party rejected the UF's proposal for forming a coordination committee to find a way out of the political impasse. The party reiterated that Deve Gowda would have to step down to facilitate any meaningful dialogue.
The Hindustan Times
UNITED FRONT PREPARES FOR FORMAL PEACE TALKS

On the basis of feelers received from the Congress, preparations were afoot in the United Front (UF) for setting up a negotiating table to avoid further precipitate action by either side. Informal consultations that started Monday, have enabled both parties to understand each other's negotiating stance. A formal communication to the Congress about the UF's March 31 resolution seeking reconsideration of withdrawal of support to the government would set the stage for authorised peace parleys aimed at evolving a mutually acceptable formula.
The Economic Times
CHAMBERS LOBBYING WITH LEADERS TO SAVE BUDGET

Industry chambers were lobbying various government and political agencies to save the budget. The Federation of Indian Chamber of Commerce and Industry (FICCI) and the Associated Chambers of Commerce and Industry (Assocham) also appealed to all parties to arrive at a consensus to salvage the 1997/98 budget which received acceptability from all quarters. The FICCI president has met the speaker of the lower house twice since the political turmoil began. Sources said he expressed concern over the pending budget and various problems industry would face if the budget was not passed.
27 PCT RISE IN IMPORTS PUSHES DEFICIT TO $5.25 BLN

The trade deficit for April-February (1996/97) stood at $5.25 billion, with exports for the period at $29.8 billion and imports at $35.05 billion. Imports witnessed 26.87 percent growth in February at $3.55 billion compared to $2.97 billion recorded in February 1996. However, exports during the month grew only 1.15 percent at an estimated $2.65 billion compared to $2.62 billion posted during February 1996. However, during the month, both exports and imports were less compared to that in January, 1997.
NEW COMMERCIAL BORROWING FACILITY NOT A FREE WINDOW

The Finance Ministry made it clear that external commercial borrowings by corporates for general corporate objectives would be allowed only as a one-time facility. A company would be allowed to access a second loan only after the first one was repaid. The clarification was a setback to industry which was euphoric over the ministry's earlier announcement that corporate borrowers would be allowed to raise long term resources of up to $200 million with a 20-year maturity and $100 million with a 10-year maturity for domestic use. The clarification means that companies would not be allowed to access this facility frequently.
PLAN FOR PASSAGE OF FINANCE BILL BEFORE APRIL 11 DROPPED

The government dropped its plan to seek the passage of the Finance Bill before April 11, when it would prove its majority in parliament. The government, which earlier sought the speaker's help in securing the passage of the bill, informed the lower house secretariat that it had decided otherwise. The politburo of the Communist Party on India (Marxist), which had serious reservations over some of the taxation proposals and whose role had become crucial for the survival of the government, was opposed to the finance minister's pressing for early clearance of the budget.
NON PERFORMING ASSET NORMS RELAXED

The Reserve Bank of India relaxed norms for classification of non-performing assets (NPAs) of financial institutions (FIs). In a circular, the RBI said only assets on which the principal component was not paid for more than four quarters in a year, need be classified as NPAs as against two quarters earlier. Another significant change was that on satisfactory performance, an NPA may be upgraded after one year. Earlier it could not be classified as a performing one for two years even if the borrower began to repay. The move would allow several cash-strapped projects to escape the NPA tag and boost profits of the FIs significantly.
Financial Express
STATE BANK ARRANGES LOANS FOR FINANCIAL INSTITUTIONS

The State Bank of India (SBI) arranged a record $2.5 billion foreign exchange loans for Indian corporates and financial institutions in 1996/97 (April-March). This was the highest amount ever arranged by SBI in the international market. In 1995/96, it had raised $1 billion in syndicated loans for Indian corporates. A majority of the deals were syndicated in the Asian loan market with transactions totalling $1.4 billion. On a stand alone basis, the bank extended short term foreign currency loans amounting to $1 billion to various corporates including private sector, blue chips and profit-making government companies.
BOMBAY COURT SANCTIONS ICICI-SCICI MERGER

The Bombay High Court sanctioned the merger of Industrial Credit & Investment Corporation (ICICI) with Shipping Credit and Investment Corporation(SCICI). The largest ever merger in the country's financial sector might be completed by April 15. The merger would be effective from April 1, 1996. Employees of the two institutions were being redeployed. The institution would seek the central bank's permission to issue shares to SCICI's non resident Indian shareholders.
INVESTORS UNHAPPY AT TATA-SIA GROUNDING

Grounding of the 24.8 billion rupee Tata-Singapore Airlines joint venture, due to the new aviation policy, has dismayed Singapore investors. The chairman of the Singapore-Indian Chamber of Commerce and Industry said they were hoping the government would clear the proposal after recommendation from the Foreign Investment Promotion Board. He said the decision made all joint ventures between Singapore and India uncertain. Observers said it could also affect ASEAN-India business initiatives. One of the issues brought up at the ASEAN-India discussion in Delhi in November and Jakarta this March was the need for an open skies policy in India.
INDUSTRY BODY TO PRESENT POLICY ON AVIATION

The industry apex body, CII, expressed concern over the negative effect on foreign direct investment (FDI) inflows in the aviation sector in the wake of the new aviation policy. The apex chamber proposed to meet government officials with its own set guidelines for foreign investment in airlines and airports. The chamber's presentation to the government would highlight examples of countries permitting FDI in domestic airlines. CII felt the policy should have taken into account the opinion of all segments of trade and business before its final decision on the policy.
Business Standard
SECTORAL INVESTMENT POLICY TO PROTECT DOMESTIC INDUSTRY

The Industry Ministry was formulating a sectoral policy for foreign direct investment. The policy would be based on the Chinese model to ensure the domestic industry was able to stand up to foreign competition. The department of industrial policy and promotion shortlisted the paper, cement, tobacco and pharmaceuticals sectors where it would promote investment for upgrading technology and, at the same time, channelise foreign investment to complement domestic investment.
PORT OPERATIONS HIT BY TRUCKERS' STRIKE

The government sought the army's help in moving goods as more than two million truck owners continued to keep their vehicles off the roads. The third day of the strike nearly brought to a halt dry cargo handling at all major ports. Bombay port was affected fully while ports on the eastern coast have been affected partially. The government asked the defence ministry to help the states in moving goods through help by the army. Meanwhile, the Delhi state government invoked the Essential Services Maintenance Act to make essential commodities available.
BOMBAY BOURSE INDEX UP 21 POINTS

The 30-share sensitive index of the Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) gained ground for the third consecutive trading day, dosing at 3,559.65 which was 21.25 points above the previous close of 3,538.40. The markets reflected improved sentiment following reports that a consensus could be evolved among political parties to pass the Finance Bill. Pivotals at BSE and the National Stock Exchange continued to move up on hopes that the budget would be passed in its totality, irrespective of which party came to power.
MOVE FOR OFFSHORE BUSINESS CENTRE IN BOMBAY

The industry apex body, CII, will present a proposal to the Maharashtra government to create an offshore financial centre in Bombay. The plan will seek to provide a base for corporates to make project financing through foreign currency loans easier and prevent the best of Indian paper moving overseas. It will involve the entry of foreign funds, financial institutions, foreign banks, investment banks and money brokers in the centre to set up offices and carry out global finance activities. All such institutions would be allowed to carry out international transactions in foreign currencies.
FINANCIAL INSTITUTIONS CAN WRITE BACK EXCESS PROVISION

The Reserve Bank of India allowed financial institutions (FIs) to write back excess provision towards depreciation on equity investments to the profit and loss account. The move was expected to boost the bottom line of FIs which had huge equity investment portfolios. The RBI said that an equal amount should also be appropriated to the capital reserve account on the liabilities side of the balance sheet in order to ensure the balance sheet was strengthened. It directed FIs to categorise their equity investments as current and long term.
The Observer
NEED TO TRIM INTEREST RATES

With the announcement of slack season credit policy due within a fortnight, the finance secretary advocated reducing interest rates. In a meeting with industrialists, he said the high rates prevailing in India were due to basic structural problems. However, he rejected arguments that Indian industry was not able to compete globally because of high cost of credit, and said the real wage rate was much below rates the world over.
